principles: Only correct document facts that are mechanically verifiable.
Keep review scope limited to the execution plan and NAV synchronization.
drivers: The document will guide future agents and generated prompts.
Command examples must match real CLI behavior.
NAV must make truth-source documents discoverable.

options.name: A: Review and fix the document inside a narrow documentation story
pros: Creates lifecycle evidence for the document review
Keeps edits scoped to the document and NAV
Allows TEST to use command and scan evidence
cons: More process overhead than a quick edit

options.name: B: Treat this as an informal note and leave the document outside story flow
cons: Leaves no lifecycle evidence for a truth-source document
Does not demonstrate that document review can use Lattice gates

options.name: C: Expand scope to execute all template and README cleanup now
pros: Would reduce known residual guidance immediately
cons: Violates the user request to review this document first
Overlaps with separate runtime/template cleanup work

chosen: A: Review and fix the document inside a narrow documentation story
rationale: Option A matches the user request for a full Lattice story review while avoiding arbitrary expansion into unrelated runtime and template cleanup.

preMortem.scenario: The review story silently fixes runtime source or README residuals
preMortem.trigger: The document scan exposes real residuals outside the approved files
preMortem.consequence: Scope expands beyond document review and collides with other active stories
preMortem.mitigation: Keep residual cleanup as follow-up execution work and only document the scan/gate here

preMortem.scenario: The document recommends a command that does not exist
preMortem.mitigation: Require help checks for Codex adapter diagnostics and verification commands

preMortem.consequence: A truth-source decision exists but normal doc discovery misses it
preMortem.mitigation: Verify NAV count and entry in TEST
